question: A 28-year-old unmarried woman at 23 weeks of pregnancy requests termination of pregnancy at a PHC in Maharashtra, citing foetal abnormality detected on ultrasound. Under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act, 2021, which statement is most accurate?

answers.text: Termination up to 24 weeks is permissible for unmarried women, but requires opinion of two registered medical practitioners for gestations beyond 20 weeks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The MTP Amendment 2021 extended the upper limit to 24 weeks for special categories including unmarried women, rape survivors, and cases with foetal abnormalities. Beyond 20 weeks, two RMP opinions are required; a State-level Medical Board decides cases above 24 weeks.

answers.text: Termination is not permissible beyond 20 weeks for unmarried women regardless of foetal abnormality

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This reflects the pre-2021 law. The MTP Amendment 2021 extended the permissible period to 24 weeks for specific categories including unmarried women and cases of foetal abnormality.

answers.text: Only a gynaecologist can approve the termination; the PHC medical officer has no authority

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Any RMP with specified training can opine under the Act. The PHC MO's role is to assess, document, and refer appropriately — the Act does not restrict this to specialists alone.

answers.text: The PCPNDT Act prohibits sex-selective termination, so all terminations after 20 weeks are automatically illegal

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The PCPNDT Act prohibits sex determination for sex-selection, not all terminations after 20 weeks. The MTP Act and PCPNDT Act address different practices and operate in parallel.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the MTP Amendment 2021. It extended the upper limit to 24 weeks for special categories and clarified the requirement for two registered medical practitioners' opinion between 20–24 weeks.
Excellent application! The MTP Amendment 2021 is a key legal change affecting community medicine practice across PHC-level facilities.
